item.title: How to Pay Solar Installers Per Job in Australia: Rate Cards
item.description:
Most solar businesses don’t fall out with their subbies over the rate. They fall out over the money arriving late, a variation nobody agreed to, or a job that got paid twice while another one never got paid at all.

When I search for how to pay installers per job, nearly everything that comes up is a software vendor’s page. You’ll find a US-focused roundup of invoicing tools (SubcontractorHub, 2026), a solar CRM’s invoicing feature page (Solar Hub CRM, n.d.) and an explainer on accounts payable automation (Vergo, n.d.). They’re all about which tool to buy. None of them tells you how to set up the pay itself.

item.title: Job Photo Capture App for Solar Installers: Auto Upload (AU)
item.description:
Most solar businesses don’t lose an audit, a warranty dispute or an STC claim because nobody took the photo. They lose it because somebody took the photo and nobody can find it. It’s sitting on a subbie’s phone, buried in a WhatsApp thread from four months ago, or saved as IMG_4471.jpg with no address, no date and no job number.

I’ve watched this happen across hundreds of businesses over twenty years. The fix isn’t a fancier camera. You need a capture workflow where photos land in the right job automatically, even when the roof is 40 minutes out of town and the phone shows one bar.

item.title: Business Interruption Insurance for Solar Installers (AU Guide)
item.description: Most solar install businesses don’t go under because of one bad job. They go under because something stops the job queue for six weeks while the wages, the ute repayments and the software subscriptions keep coming out every fortnight. A storm takes out the shed and the stock in it, your lead installer does a knee coming off a ladder, or a container of inverters sits on a wharf. The work is still there, but you can’t do it, so nothing gets invoiced.

item.title: Job Costing for Solar Installers: Quoted vs Real Margin
item.description: Here is the uncomfortable truth about job costing on solar installs: the margin you quote and the margin you keep are two different numbers, and most installers never sit down to work out the gap. The quote is a forecast. The real margin only shows up weeks later, once the panels are on, the sparky is paid, the certificates are sold and the callbacks are done. By then you have already moved on to the next job, and the leak never gets found.
